clue.text: Dress strap that's hard to modify

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
to modify something is to alter it

explanation.surface: A dressmaker complains that a shoulder strap is difficult to adjust.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter is a strap passing round the neck to hold up the bodice of a backless dress or top.

clue.text: He finally dispatched a band with scores

definitions.text: He finally dispatched a band with scores

parts.words: He finally dispatched a band with scores
parts.note: reads like a hitman disposing of a music group with its sheet music, but the band is the Forty Thieves of the Arabian Nights tale, forty being two scores

explanation.surface: Someone at last gets rid of a musical group along with its sheet music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks musical beside 'band', but a score is twenty, so 'a band with scores' is a gang numbering forty: the thieves of the Arabian Nights story, whose hero sees them finished off.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcutter of the Arabian Nights tale outwits and ends up rid of the forty thieves whose cave he discovers.

clue.text: I sit up penning short draft law for capital

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece holds the other inside it
in a down clue, up means the words I and sit are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for a draft law is cut off

parts.note: a bill is a draft of a law put before parliament

explanation.surface: Someone sits up late drafting legislation for the nation's seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the letters bottom to top; 'short' docks the final letter; 'penning' encloses the shortened bill within the reversed letters, after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tbilisi is the capital city of Georgia.

clue.text: For book, attempt to rectify initial fault?

definitions.meaning: to book a table or seat is to secure it in advance
in tennis, after a first serve is faulted, the player serves again

explanation.surface: A tennis player wonders whether a second go will make up for a first slip, all for a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-SERVE, serve again, which is what a tennis player does after a fault on the first serve.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve a hotel room is the same as to book it ahead.

clue.text: Small bird part-exchanged for this vegetable

indicators.note: the two parts of the bird's name swap places, as in trading one part for the other

parts.note: a peachick is a young peafowl

explanation.surface: A young bird is traded in, motor-dealer style, for a pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part-exchanged' suggests a car trade-in; here the halves PEA and CHICK swap ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickpea, or garbanzo, is a legume eaten as a vegetable in hummus and curries.

clue.text: Author listened to poet showing courage

indicators.note: listened to means the author's name is heard rather than seen spelt

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist
Thomas Hood, the English poet of comic and social verse

explanation.surface: A novelist hears a poet's work and shows bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: HARDI only sounds like Hardy; the spelling follows the ending -ihood as in likelihood.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardihood is boldness or daring, a willingness to face danger.

clue.text: Sound production of Cat on a Hot Tin Roof?

definitions.text: Sound production of Cat on a Hot Tin Roof?

parts.words: Sound production of Cat on a Hot Tin Roof?
parts.note: reads as a good staging of the Tennessee Williams play, but taken literally it is the noise a distressed cat on a scorching roof would make

explanation.surface: A theatre critic praises a solid staging of the Tennessee Williams drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' seems to mean sturdy and 'production' a staging, but read literally it is the noise a cat makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To caterwaul is to howl or screech like a cat on heat or in pain.

clue.text: Yes, Pound contrived metre like Eliot, for instance

indicators.note: contrived means put together artfully, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: fodder
fodder

explanation.surface: Ezra Pound wrote in a metre like that of his fellow modernist T. S. Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound and Eliot look like the two modernist poets, but the Eliot meant is George Eliot, the pen name of Mary Ann Evans.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was the assumed name under which the novelist Mary Ann Evans published.

clue.text: So be it, man? Turns out just the opposite

indicators.note: turns out means the words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker says amen to something, then finds the opposite happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So be it' is what amen means; the Latin phrase means may it not be an omen, the opposite wish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is said to ward off ill luck, a hope that something will not come true, the reverse of agreeing it should.

clue.text: Skirt area of France

definitions.meaning: the south of France is known as le ...

explanation.surface: A fashion note about a skirt from a French region.
explanation.definitionFit: A midi is a skirt reaching mid-calf; le Midi is the southern region of France.

clue.text: Depressed, unlike St. Louis?

definitions.meaning: Lindbergh's plane was the Spirit of St Louis, so something unlike St Louis would lack a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone feels down, unlike the cheerful people of a Missouri city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spirit of St Louis was the plane in which Charles Lindbergh first flew solo across the Atlantic in 1927.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispirited person lacks vigour and courage, feeling low.

clue.text: Sharp punishment that is right

parts.note: a rap, as in a rap on the knuckles, is a punishment
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A stern rebuke is deemed justified.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender pointed sword, a sharp weapon.

clue.text: It's eventually blown up by spies

definitions.text: It's eventually blown up by spies

parts.words: It's eventually blown up by spies
parts.note: suggests sabotage by agents, but blown up means enlarged: spies magnify a tiny photographed document to read it

explanation.surface: Something is finally destroyed by secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown up' looks like an explosion; it means photographically enlarged.
explanation.definitionFit: A microdot is a photograph reduced to the size of a dot, used by spies to hide documents.

clue.text: Election promises a most fine outcome

indicators.note: the outcome of the words is a new form, a signal that they are rearranged

parts.note: fodder
fodder

explanation.surface: A party's pledges promise a splendid result.
explanation.definitionFit: A party manifesto sets out the policies it pledges to deliver if elected.

clue.text: Male corgi harassed sheep very little

indicators.note: harassed means badgered and thrown into disorder, so the letters of corgi are jumbled

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A male dog chases sheep a tiny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A microgram is a millionth of a gram, an extremely small amount.

clue.text: Strangely, I turn into what I eat

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone muses that they are becoming whatever they consume.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment is the food taken in by a body.

clue.text: Pretentious accommodation provided before university term

parts.note: a flat is a set of rooms to live in
Lent is the spring term at some British universities, such as Cambridge

explanation.surface: A student is given lodgings before the start of term at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Lent term is the name some British universities give to their spring term.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatulent prose is pompous and inflated, full of empty wind.

clue.text: Devil's about to ruin one model of goodness

indicators.note: about means going round, so the devil's name surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Satan is the Devil; the possessive here has the sense has
to mar is to spoil or ruin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The Devil is about to destroy one paragon of virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as is going to, but 'about' is the container indicator and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A good Samaritan, from the parable, is anyone who generously helps a stranger in need.

clue.text: Vietnamese region giving back spiritual nourishment

indicators.note: giving back means the word for the food is returned, read in reverse

parts.note: manna is the food from heaven, figuratively spiritual sustenance

explanation.surface: A region of Vietnam returns religious sustenance.
explanation.definitionFit: Annam was the central region of Vietnam under French rule.

clue.text: Sort of coat about ending on waist?

definitions.text: Sort of coat about ending on waist?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are rearranged
ending on means only the last letter of waist is taken

explanation.surface: A tailor asks what kind of coat finishes at the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a garment whose name is a rearranged coat plus the last letter of 'waist', and which itself ends around the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short surplice, an over-garment worn by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: Trader or soldier, according to Jaques?

definitions.meaning: a dealer who buys from producers and sells on
in As You Like It, Jaques lists the seven ages of man, and the soldier is the fourth, the middle one

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a merchant or a soldier figures in Shakespeare's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaques's 'All the world's a stage' speech gives seven ages; the soldier is fourth of seven.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary dealer stands between producer and buyer.

clue.text: Distinctive speech featured in media lectures

indicators.note: featured in means the letters appear inside the phrase media lectures

explanation.surface: Regional accents are a topic in talks about broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is the local form of a language with its own words and pronunciation.

clue.text: Make amends for former head introducing unit of Latin

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: introducing means bringing one piece inside another

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
I is one in Roman numerals, the Latin way of writing a unit

explanation.surface: An ex-headmaster begins teaching a module of Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former head' suggests an ex-headteacher; EX and PATE are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a sin is to atone for it.

clue.text: Display opening for Charles de Gaulle, perhaps

parts.note: to air views is to display them
a port, as in porthole, is an opening

explanation.surface: An exhibition opening for a French statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: The French president is named, but the definition is the Paris hub named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles de Gaulle is the main international hub serving Paris.

clue.text: One must go to get this article

definitions.text: One must go to get this article

parts.words: One must go to get this article
parts.note: sounds like an errand to fetch an item, but go means die: a newspaper piece written about someone after their death

explanation.surface: Someone has to make a trip to pick up an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' means die and 'article' a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper writes a notice of a person's life after their death.

clue.text: Currently commemorated physicist

parts.note: a scientist whose name lives on in the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A scientist is being honoured at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' seems to mean at present; it means in electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: André-Marie Ampère, the French physicist, gave his name to the SI unit of electric current.

clue.text: Imitation diamond having tint of great water

parts.note: the Rhine is a great European river; of makes it possessive, the Rhine's
a tone is a shade or tint

explanation.surface: A fake gem with the tint of a fine sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great water' suggests the sea, but is the river Rhine, where these paste gems were first made.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinestone is a paste or glass gem made to look like a diamond.

clue.text: Superior to join at work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A boss asks a subordinate to join in at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed on top of another is above it, higher up.

clue.text: No theatre award given after second dull routine

indicators.note: given after means the following pieces come after the word for second

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
taken as written
a Tony is an American award for theatre

explanation.surface: A show wins no theatre prize after a moment, a tedious routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious sameness of routine is described as humdrum repetition.

clue.text: Behave like consumer in attempt to get bargain

indicators.note: in means the act of eating goes inside the word for an attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a consumer eats

explanation.surface: A shopper behaves like a consumer while trying to get a good deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' suggests a shopper; here it is one who eats.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is an agreement or deal between parties.
